primitives.name: Bradley-Terry Win Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Bradley–Terry paired-comparison model for win probability: logit(π_{i,j}) = β_i - β_j + α (α = home advantage).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\pi_{i,j}': 'probability of team i beating team j (dimensionless)', '\\beta_i': 'strength parameter for team i (dimensionless)', '\\beta_j': 'strength parameter for team j (dimensionless)', '\\alpha': 'home advantage parameter (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Teams' strengths are additive in log-odds space; home advantage is constant across matchups.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When team strength parameters become unstable due to insufficient data or overfitting.

layer2.mapping: GSI employs Bradley-Terry for estimating team quality with Bayesian priors; GSE applies it in a rolling window to compute time-varying team ratings.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of win predictions against baseline (always pick home team).

primitives.name: Margin of Victory Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Margin-of-victory model: μ_{i,j} = δ_i - δ_j + λ (λ = home edge in points).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mu_{i,j}': 'expected point margin between teams i and j (points)', '\\delta_i': 'offensive strength of team i (points)', '\\delta_j': 'offensive strength of team j (points)', '\\lambda': 'home field advantage in points (points)'}
primitives.assumptions: Point margins are linearly related to offensive strengths with fixed home bias.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When variance in scoring exceeds linear model assumptions or when teams have very different playing styles.

layer2.mapping: GSI derives MOV estimates from Bradley-Terry parameters; GSE uses MOV to refine rating volatility and adjust decay rates.
layer2.telemetry: Prediction error in point spread accuracy.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When increasing sample size yields diminishing returns in predictive accuracy.

layer2.telemetry: Cumulative accuracy gain per game added to training set.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper lies in quantifying how much information each game contributes toward understanding team strength. This is modeled through Bradley-Terry logit regression where team strengths β_i and β_j are compared, adjusted by a fixed home advantage α. The model assumes that win probabilities depend additively on these latent strengths, making it suitable for ranking teams based on match outcomes. The margin-of-victory extension introduces an additional layer by modeling expected score differences, assuming linearity in offensive capabilities with a home bias term λ. However, the paper’s methodology uses random within-season sampling which introduces temporal leakage—future games are used to estimate past team strength—a flawed approach for deployment. To adapt this for GSE, we must replace this with a chronological rolling-origin evaluation that respects causality. The key innovation is to apply temporal decay kernels to the Bradley-Terry parameters, allowing for dynamic updates of team ratings while preserving stability. This enables GSE to make real-time decisions grounded in evolving team performance without retroactive contamination. The plateau analysis provides a stopping criterion for when sufficient data has been collected to reliably rank teams, ensuring that GSE does not over-train on early-season noise. The failure mode arises if the model assumes stationarity in team dynamics beyond what is empirically supported, especially in leagues with frequent roster changes or high variance in play styles.
